# Vancouver Daily News
> **Ninety-six thousand two hundred thirty-eight patients now wait for B.C. surgery.**

Separately, a Canadian citizen was questioned for hours at the Point Roberts crossing on the way home from Tsawwassen, and Canpotex is putting $500 million into a North Vancouver port terminal.

### Top Stories
**96,238 patients waiting for surgery, SecondStreet data show: Vancouver Sun**
Canadian think tank SecondStreet.org released data showing 96,238 patients are waiting for surgery in British Columbia, up 8.4 per cent since 2022. The Vancouver Sun's report frames the province as in "crisis" and says the number of patients waiting for surgery, and the number dying on wait-lists, are both increasing. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/bc-crisis-number-patients-waiting-surgery-increases-data-show)

**Canadian citizen questioned for hours at Point Roberts: CBC British Columbia**
Paige Adamson, a Canadian citizen, was on her way home from a birthday dinner in Tsawwassen on September 15 when she was stopped at the Point Roberts border crossing and questioned about voting for hours. CBC reports that lawyers are raising concerns about vulnerabilities Canadians face while living in the United States, especially over being registered to vote. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/canadian-detained-at-bc-border-for-hours-9.7359371?cmp=rss)

**Canpotex puts $500 million into a North Vancouver terminal: Global BC**
Canpotex, a Saskatchewan-based potash exporter, is spending $500 million to help fund the refurbishment and replacement of equipment at a Port of Vancouver shipping terminal in North Vancouver. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12073272/potash-company-invests-north-vancouver-terminal/)

**Parole board grants Shane Ertmoed a 60-day unescorted leave: Global BC**
The parole board has granted Shane Ertmoed a 60-day unescorted leave to take cooking classes. The Vancouver Sun reports he is serving a life sentence for abducting, sexually assaulting and killing 10-year-old Heather Thomas in October 2000. Heather's mother, Jody Aspin, told Global News she was outraged by the decision and said she is made to continuously suffer. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12073895/shane-ertmoed-unescorted-leave/)

### City & Province
**White Rock Mayor Megan Knight confirmed in Surrey South: CBC British Columbia**
White Rock Mayor Megan Knight is confirmed as the B.C. Conservative candidate in Surrey South. CBC reports there is no law preventing someone from running in both municipal and provincial races at the same time. In May last year, the B.C. government passed legislation banning people from holding both offices simultaneously. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/white-rock-mayor-election-9.7359492?cmp=rss)

**Six decades of Treaty 8 recordings repatriated to Dane-zaa people: CBC British Columbia**
Six decades of Treaty 8 history have been repatriated to Dane-zaa people in northern British Columbia. Anthropologists from the Ridington family began working alongside Dane-zaa elders in the 1960s to record traditional songs, oral histories, and everyday life spanning six decades. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/ridington-dane-zaa-archive-treaty-8-repatriation-9.7359061?cmp=rss)

**Man, 23, awarded almost $5 million over a Burnaby pool fall: Vancouver Sun**
A man, 23, has been awarded almost $5 million after being injured as a child in a fall at a Burnaby pool. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/man-awarded-5-million-fall-burnaby-pool)

### Getting Around
Highway 1 in Langley still has full overnight directional closures between the 264 Street exit area and about 380 metres northwest of Exit 61 to 216 Street, from 9:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m., through Sunday, September 27, with detours via crossovers. In Delta, the Exit 29 River Road ramp stays closed from 10:00 p.m. to 1:00 p.m. the next day, every day, until October 1, and on Highway 1 eastbound lanes are shifted north of the median around 256th Street and Lefeuvre Road and remain closed 24/7 until October 31. Highway 91A is down to one lane each way on overnight bridge maintenance until November 15, and another Highway 1 work zone holds single-lane traffic both ways overnight with a 60 km/h limit until December 15. No watches or warnings are in effect. Vancouver was mainly clear and 11.5°C; Saturday is a mix of sun and cloud, west wind 20 km/h becoming light this morning, high 16, UV index 4, then a low of 8, with Sunday mainly sunny and a high of 16 before a cloudy Monday, also high 16. Source: [drivebc.ca](https://www.drivebc.ca/) Source: [weather.gc.ca](https://weather.gc.ca/rss/weather/49.245_-123.115_e.xml)

### Sports
**B.C. Lions beat the Saskatchewan Roughriders 31-24: 3DownNation**
The B.C. Lions beat the Saskatchewan Roughriders 31-24 on Friday night at BC Place and took the regular-season series two games to one. Both clubs are 8-6, with B.C. second in the West on the tiebreaker; the Lions have won seven of their last eight, and Saskatchewan is 2-4 in its last six after a 6-2 start. Nathan Rourke, 28, was 22 of 28 for 375 yards and four touchdowns with no interceptions, added three rushes for 37 yards, and finished with 412 yards of offence. In the fourth quarter he broke Caleb Sanders's tackle, eluded Mike Rose and James Vaughters, and threw 59 yards to Justin McInnis.

**Canucks claim Leevi Merilainen off waivers: Global BC**
The Vancouver Canucks have claimed goaltender Leevi Merilainen off waivers from the Ottawa Senators. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12073352/canucks-claim-merilainen-off-waivers-from-senators/)

### What's On
**UBCP/ACTRA nominees listed for November 21 awards: Vancouver Sun**
The UBCP/ACTRA performers union has announced its 2026 nominees for the annual B.C. and Yukon awards, to be given out on November 21. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/entertainment/nominations-annual-bc-and-yukon-awards)

### Both Sides: Whether local candidates should take up the provincial argument
Premier David Eby, asked Wednesday about election timing by CBC Early Edition host Stephen Quinn, said concurrent votes "will give an opportunity for local government leaders to pick a side here as well," Les Leyne reports in the Times Colonist. A provincial election day is set for October 24; Tom Fletcher reports Eby called it on September 22 outside Government House in Victoria.

Eby's case, in that Quinn interview, is that local leaders now face the same choice he wants provincial voters to face. He asked whether they are "on the side for their communities, building out the infrastructure" and "doing that work with the federal government," or "advocates and supporters of the Conservative approach of doubling down on the old way, when we were too closely tied to the U.S., fighting unnecessary culture wars, dividing people and cutting quality programs." He said, "I think that choice is as relevant for local leaders as it is for the provincial government."

The case for keeping municipal campaigns on municipal ground comes from the Union of B.C. Municipalities. Delegates passed an emergency resolution urging Eby to respect the integrity of the local votes and not override municipal issues currently up for debate by calling a provincial election. Leyne reports various mayors were offended by Tuesday's call, particularly because Eby had been asked at the convention to wait his turn. He appeared there, said he would consider it, said he understood their anxiety, and said no decision had been made. Four days later, he called the election.

Both the premier's ask and the municipal resolution sit on the same calendar: local campaigns are underway, and provincial election day is October 24, 2026. Source: [timescolonist.com](https://www.timescolonist.com/opinion/les-leyne-eby-urges-municipal-candidates-to-pick-a-side-12824474) Source: [westernstandard.news](https://www.westernstandard.news/opinion/fletcher-david-ebys-anti-trump-strategy-reveals-his-desperation/77336)

# Vancouver Daily News
> **Burnaby schools lost internal networks and phone lines in a cyber incident.**

**What You Need to Know:** Burnaby schools are dealing with a cyber incident that took out internal networks and phone lines, and families are being warned about scams. A court has left a 229-home Cambie rental approval in place without below-market units. The Canucks lost a preseason game at Rogers Arena, and Filip Chytil left with a shoulder injury.

### Top Stories
**Cyberattack on Burnaby School District triggers widespread disruption:** CBC British Columbia
A message to families said internal network services and phone lines had been impacted. Parents are being warned not to fall victim to cybercrime that could be committed using stolen information. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/cyber-attack-burnaby-schools-9.7357905?cmp=rss)

**1.2 million British Columbians have no family doctor:** CBC British Columbia
The B.C. NDP says its policies have connected a million people across B.C. to a family doctor. CBC British Columbia reports that 1.2 million British Columbians still have no family doctor. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/family-doctors-bc-ndp-9.7356810?cmp=rss)

**New poll shows two-thirds not in favour of an early B.C. election:** CBC British Columbia
Angus Reid Institute data shows two-thirds of respondents are not in favour of an early election. In that data, the B.C. Conservatives, led by Lorne Doerkson, hold 43 per cent support among respondents, an eight-point lead over the NDP at 35 per cent. The Vancouver Sun reports that a competing poll shows the NDP ahead, and that voters remain divided as the campaign continues. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/new-poll-shows-two-thirds-not-in-favour-of-early-election-9.7357659?cmp=rss) Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/bc-election-polls-conservatives-early-lead)

### City & Province
**NDP lose four cabinet ministers, including David Eby's top lieutenant:** Vancouver Sun
The Vancouver Sun reports that the NDP has lost four cabinet ministers, including David Eby's top lieutenant. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/ndp-lose-four-cabinet-ministers-including-ebys-top-lieutenant)

**Eby promises Built in B.C. and Canada procurement rules:** Global BC
On Thursday morning, BC NDP Leader David Eby said the party will bring in new Built in B.C. and Canada procurement rules for public infrastructure projects. That remains a campaign promise, not a rule now in force. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12072022/bc-election-campaign-day-three-ndp-trump-trade-war-bc-greens/)

**SRO owner says City of Vancouver failed to act before Powell Street fire:** Global BC
SRO owner Bob Fontaine says the City of Vancouver failed to act before the Powell Street fire.

**Raccoon euthanized after leg caught in trap in Langley:** Global BC
A raccoon was euthanized after its leg was caught in a trap in a Langley neighbourhood. The Fur-Bearers is offering a one-thousand-dollar reward for information leading to the identification and conviction of the person or people who set the trap. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12072353/raccoon-euthanized-leg-trap-langley-neighbourhood/)

### Getting Around
DriveBC says paving on Highway 99 runs Tuesday, September 29, and Wednesday, September 30, from 11 p.m. to 6 a.m., with the road closed and a single northbound lane alternating for emergency vehicles and transit only; use the Ironworkers Memorial Bridge. In Delta, the Exit 29 River Road ramp is closed from 10 p.m. to 1 p.m. the next day, every day, through October 1. On Highway 1 in Langley, watch for full overnight directional closures from 8:30 p.m. to 10:30 a.m. on Saturday, through September 27, with detours via crossovers. Eastbound Highway 1 lanes stay closed around 256th Street and Lefeuvre Road, with traffic shifted north of the median, through October 31.
Environment Canada has no watches or warnings in effect for Vancouver. Current conditions are mostly cloudy and 12.2 degrees. Friday brings periods of rain, with wind becoming northwest at 30 km/h gusting to 50 this morning, and a temperature steady near 12. Friday night, rain ends, then it is cloudy with a 60 per cent chance of showers before partly cloudy skies, wind west at 20 km/h gusting to 40, and a temperature near 11. Saturday is a mix of sun and cloud with a high of 15; Saturday night is clear with a low of 7; Sunday is sunny with a high of 17. Source: [drivebc.ca](https://www.drivebc.ca/) Source: [weather.gc.ca](https://weather.gc.ca/rss/weather/49.245_-123.115_e.xml)

### Sports
**Oilers 2, Canucks 1 in preseason at Rogers Arena:** NHL.com
The Edmonton Oilers beat a near full-strength Canucks lineup 2-1 on Thursday at Rogers Arena. Isaac Howard scored at 3:58 of the first period and assisted on Quinn Hutson's goal before the five-minute mark of the second; the Canucks scored on the power play 1:33 later. Tristan Jarry made 25 saves, and the Oilers are 3-0-0 in exhibition play. Edmonton opens the regular season Tuesday at home against the Canucks. Sportsnet reports that Filip Chytil suffered a shoulder injury in the game. Source: [nhl.com](https://www.nhl.com/oilers/news/game-recap-oilers-2-canucks-1-preseason-09-24-26) Source: [sportsnet.ca](https://www.sportsnet.ca/nhl/article/canucks-filip-chytil-exits-after-colliding-with-official/)

### What's On
**Hakka youth fire dragon ritual and cultural festival:** Vancouver Is Awesome
A Hakka youth fire dragon ritual and cultural festival is coming to Chinatown this weekend. Source: [vancouverisawesome.com](https://www.vancouverisawesome.com/events-and-entertainment/hakka-youth-fire-dragon-ritual-and-cultural-festival-sept-2026-12820101)

**Police vs. Fire charity hockey game in Surrey:** Surrey Now-Leader
A police-versus-fire charity hockey game in Surrey is set for October 10, and the Surrey Now-Leader reports it will get competitive. Source: [surreynowleader.com](https://surreynowleader.com/2026/09/24/police-vs-fire-charity-hockey-game-in-surrey-will-get-competitive-oct-10/)

### Both Sides: Below-market homes in a Cambie rental approval
Vancouver's approval of 229 secured purpose-built rental homes near King Edward Station, with no below-market units, is what the court was asked to undo. The Cambie Corridor Neighbourhood Association sought to rescind the approval. The City of Vancouver and developer Sightline Properties were the respondents. Justice Morellato of the Supreme Court of British Columbia dismissed the association's challenge last week.

The association's case is that the approval should be overturned. Daily Hive reports the bid targeted a low-rise secured rental project after council proceeded with no below-market rental homes included.

The city's case, as the court stated it, is that the process was fair and council's decision was reasonable. Council unanimously approved the rezoning in July 2025. Sightline's reason for building rental, as set out in the ruling, is practical: it had planned 46 townhomes expected to sell for 2 million to 2.3 million dollars each, obtained permits in 2022, demolished the houses and started excavation, then had no pre-sales in a weakening market and shifted to rental after provincial changes that encouraged more density near SkyTrain.

Both sides are dealing with the same project: 520-590 West 29th Avenue and 4510-4550 Ash Street, about a 10-minute walk south of the Canada Line station, with two six-storey buildings and two townhouse blocks. The unit count went from 230 at rezoning to 229 when the development permit was issued in December 2025, and below-market homes were not part of the approval. The dismissal leaves that approval in place. Source: [dailyhive.com](https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/520-590-west-29th-avenue-4510-4550-ash-street-vancouver-rental-housing-sightline-cambie-corridor-legal-challenge)

# Vancouver Daily News
> **Two people died on Highway 1 in Burnaby, with one person arrested.**

**What You Need to Know:** A Highway 1 crash in Burnaby killed two people, sent one person to hospital, and ended with one person arrested. Vancouver has recorded its sixth homicide of 2026 after a man died in CRAB Park. A fire at D Dutchmen Dairy killed around 40 calves, and the Canucks have put Thatcher Demko on injured reserve.

### Top Stories
**Two people killed, one arrested after Highway 1 crash in Burnaby: CBC**
Two people were killed in a crash on Highway 1 in Burnaby, CBC reports. One person was arrested. A separate CBC report says one person was sent to hospital. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/rcmp-serious-collision-hwy-1-burnaby-bc-9.7354982)

**Vancouver sees sixth homicide of 2026 after man dies in CRAB Park: Global News**
Vancouver has recorded its sixth homicide of 2026 after a man died in CRAB Park, Global News reports. Officers were called to the park in the Downtown Eastside early Wednesday after someone reported a man in medical distress. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12070755/vancouver-6th-homicide-2026-crab-park/)

**About 40 calves dead in fire at D Dutchmen Dairy: CBC**
D Dutchmen Dairy says an overnight fire devastated three structures on the farm and killed around 40 calves, CBC reports. The dairy is a B.C. highway stop. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/d-dutchmen-dairy-fire-sicamous-bc-9.7356745?cmp=rss)

**Vancouver student climate lawsuit heads to trial: Vancouver Sun**
Zoe Grames-Webb joined a youth climate lawsuit in 2019 at age 13, and the case is going to trial in Vancouver seven years later, the Vancouver Sun reports. The Sun links her fight to health issues from wildfire smoke. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/vancouver-student-fights-back-after-wildfire-smoke-causes-health-issues)

### City & Province
**Mount Jack wildfire north of Sooke still out of control: CBC**
The Mount Jack wildfire on southern Vancouver Island, north of Sooke, is still classified as out of control by the B.C. Wildfire Service, CBC reports. It was discovered on September 20 and has grown to at least 210 hectares. Part of the Galloping Goose Trail has been closed as a precaution. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/mount-jack-wildfire-remains-out-of-control-9.7297493?cmp=rss)

**Faulder resident says life is ashes after wildfire: Global News**
Joel Patan says his life is ashes as he sifts the ruins of his home, incinerated last month along with most structures in the small community of Faulder, Global News reports. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12071400/bc-wildfire-recovery/)

### Getting Around
No watches or warnings are in effect. On Highway 1 in Langley, traffic is shifted north of the median around 256th Street and crosses back around Lefeuvre Road, with the existing eastbound lanes closed around the clock through October 31, DriveBC says. The Exit 29 River Road ramp in Delta is closed from 10 p.m. to 1 p.m. the next day, every day, through October 1, and traffic on 264th Street is shifted west onto a new bridge, with a detour, through October 17., and on September 29 and 30 Highway 99 paving runs from 11 p.m. to 6 a.m., with the highway closed and a single northbound lane alternating for emergency vehicles and transit only; DriveBC says use the Ironworkers Memorial Bridge. Thursday becomes cloudy, with rain late this afternoon, a northwest wind of 20 km/h gusting to 40, and a high of 17; Thursday night is rain with a low of 13, Friday brings periods of rain with the temperature steady near 14 and a northwest wind of 30 km/h gusting to 50 near noon, and Saturday is sunny with a high of 17. Source: [drivebc.ca](https://www.drivebc.ca/) Source: [weather.gc.ca](https://weather.gc.ca/rss/weather/49.245_-123.115_e.xml)

### Sports
**Demko placed on injured reserve with hip injury: Yardbarker**
Thatcher Demko has been placed on injured reserve with a hip injury, and the expectation now is that he will not be ready to start the 2026-27 season, Yardbarker reports. The Canucks had already said he would not be a full participant at training camp, with Kevin Lankinen expected to start in his place. Demko played 23 games in 2024-25 and 20 last season before hip surgery. The priority is getting him healthy, not setting a return date. Sportsnet reported that Lankinen is ready to shoulder the load again, and he looked good in the team's 3-1 preseason loss to the Calgary Flames. Source: [yardbarker.com](https://www.yardbarker.com/nhl/articles/canucks_get_some_bad_news_about_thatcher_demko/s1_17758_44343876)

**Lions reshuffle secondary for Roughriders amid suspensions: 3DownNation**
The B.C. Lions host the Saskatchewan Roughriders on Friday, September 25, with kickoff at 10:30 p.m. EDT, on TSN in Canada and CFL+ internationally, 3DownNation reports. The Lions are 7-6 and the Roughriders are 8-5, and both teams were on a bye last week. Ronald Kent Jr. and Canadian safety Josh Hagerty will each serve suspensions for incidents in the Week 15 win over the Montreal Alouettes, while cornerbacks Garry Peters and C.J. Coldon remain out with injuries. Robert Carter Jr., 23, signed Tuesday after his release from the Indianapolis Colts, will start at boundary cornerback. Cristophe Beaulieu moves from nickel to field halfback, Deontai Williams returns to nickel, and Stantley Thomas-Oliver steps in at field cornerback. Lorenzo Mauldin IV is back in the defensive-end rotation, and Chris Oladokun will dress as the third-string quarterback after the release of Chase Brice. Source: [3downnation.com](https://3downnation.com/2026/09/24/b-c-lions-reshuffle-secondary-versus-riders-amid-injuries-suspensions/)

**Canucks face Oilers in third pre-season game: The Hockey News**
The Vancouver Canucks play the Edmonton Oilers on Thursday night in their third game of the 2026 pre-season, The Hockey News reports. After significant cuts since Tuesday's game against the Calgary Flames, Vancouver is icing a more experienced lineup. The Edmonton Journal reports that Edmonton starts Tristan Jarry in net, with Spencer Stastney and Ty Emberson on defence, and otherwise an almost full AHL lineup. Connor Clattenburg makes his debut after missing games because of injury. Source: [thehockeynews.com](https://thehockeynews.com/nhl/vancouver-canucks/game-day/canucks-projected-lineup-for-game-3-of-the-2026-pre-season-versus-the-edmonton-oilers) Source: [edmontonjournal.com](https://edmontonjournal.com/sports/hockey/nhl/cult-of-hockey/edmonton-oilers-fan-favourite-will-at-last-take-the-ice-against-vancouver-canucks-tonight)

### Both Sides: An early provincial vote beside municipal campaigns
British Columbians vote in a provincial election on October 24, two years after the last vote kept the B.C. NDP in power, the Vancouver Sun reports. The contested question is what that early call does to municipal campaigns already underway.

Dan Fumano reports in the Vancouver Sun that some Vancouver candidates are leaning into the overlap. Their strongest reason, as he describes it, is opportunity: a provincial campaign beside a civic one is a chance to make political hay, and to tie a local race to the bigger ballot.

Other candidates, Fumano reports, rail against the call. Their strongest reason is that overlapping elections bring confusion and distraction. Alec Lazenby reports in the Vancouver Sun, in a piece listed by CityHallWatch, that the snap election throws a curveball into municipal campaigns. Vaughn Palmer's Vancouver Sun column, as listed by CityHallWatch, is headlined as Eby about to call a totally unnecessary B.C. election. Palmer also reports that Doerkson lost no time dealing with Premier David Eby's allegation of Conservatives' Trump leanings. Yesterday Eby cited an existential Trump threat in calling the vote.

Both sides are operating from the same calendar: a provincial ballot on October 24 while municipal campaigns continue. The next dated step those reports name is that October 24 vote. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/explainer-parties-running-october-bc-election) Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/opinion/columnists/how-some-vancouver-candidates-are-leaning-into-the-snap-bc-election-call-while-others-rail-against-it) Source: [cityhallwatch.wordpress.com](https://cityhallwatch.wordpress.com/2026/09/24/ucs-117-king-david-goes-into-battle/) Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/opinion/columnists/vaughn-palmer-doerkson-loses-no-time-dealing-with-ebys-allegation-of-conservatives-trump-leanings)

# Vancouver Daily News
> **Premier David Eby has called a snap provincial election for October 24, citing an existential U.S. trade threat.**

**What You Need to Know:** Premier David Eby called a snap B.C. election for October 24, framing it around U.S. trade tensions. The District of Squamish rejected a proposed 10-year, $142-million tax deal with Woodfibre LNG. A Vancouver investment firm will acquire eight Accent Inns and Hotel Zed properties across the province by the end of November.

### What This Show Covers
This is a short morning brief for people who live in Metro Vancouver. It covers what council and the province decided, what those decisions mean for getting around today, how the local teams did, what is on, and one contested local issue presented with the strongest case on each side. The brief is read by Mira, the network's AI host. Stories are chosen and written by software from named local newsrooms and public data sources such as DriveBC and Environment Canada, and every item names its source. The one thing it will not do is speculate about people—no guesses about anyone's motives, guilt, health or private life, and no endorsements at election time. Vancouver Daily News is part of the Nerra Network, an independent, ad-free network of shows at nerranetwork.com. Listeners are invited to visit the site for the full schedule.

### Top Stories
**Eby calls early provincial election on Oct. 24:** My Cariboo Now. Premier David Eby called a snap provincial election for October 24. He cited an existential threat from U.S. trade tensions as the reason for the early vote. Opposition parties have begun reorganizing ahead of the date. British Columbia's political scene is undergoing rapid restructuring as parties adjust to the October 24 date. NDP Leader David Eby framed the vote as necessary to respond to the threat posed by U.S. trade policy. The Conservative Party of B.C. has seen substantial turnover with over a dozen MLAs quitting or being expelled from caucus since August amid internal disputes. Today Peter Milobar and six other MLAs from the breakaway CentreBC party rejoined the Conservatives while Elenore Sturko remained with CentreBC and became its leader. Brent Chapman left the Conservatives to join OneBC. Kerry-Lynne Findlay resigned as leader less than four months after taking the role and Cariboo-Chilcotin MLA Lorne Doerkson took over as interim leader. Source: [mycariboonow.com](https://www.mycariboonow.com/316414/news/politics/eby-calls-early-provincial-election-on-oct-24/)

**District of Squamish rejects $142M Woodfibre LNG deal:** CBC British Columbia. The District of Squamish council turned down a negotiated 10-year tax settlement that would have delivered $142 million from Woodfibre LNG to the Sea-to-Sky community. The decision ends the proposed agreement. The settlement would have seen Woodfibre LNG contribute the funds over the decade in exchange for tax certainty. Council voted against the package after negotiations concluded. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/142m-woodfibre-lng-tax-deal-denied-by-district-of-squamish-council-9.7354771?cmp=rss)

**Vancouver company to acquire all eight Accent Inns and Hotel Zed hotels:** Daily Hive Vancouver. Synvest Group of Companies will buy the eight Accent Inns and Hotel Zed properties across British Columbia with the transfer expected at the end of November. The hotels total roughly 800 rooms. All existing bookings will be honoured and operations continue normally. The acquisition covers five Accent Inns properties in Richmond, Burnaby, Victoria, Kelowna and Kamloops plus Hotel Zed locations in Victoria, Kelowna and Tofino along with the ROAR restaurant at Hotel Zed Tofino. The largest property is Accent Inns Vancouver Airport in Richmond with over 200 rooms. Mandy Farmer CEO of the selling company said the day was emotional and that it mattered to find a new owner who understood the company culture. Azim Virani founder and principal of Synvest said the family has always viewed hospitality as being about people and that Synvest wants to work with existing teams to preserve the established approach. Source: [dailyhive.com](https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/accent-inns-hotel-zed-synvest-acquisition)

**VPD Seizes Record 328.55 kg Cocaine Worth $5.8M in Shipping Container:** VancouverPD. Vancouver police seized 328.55 kilograms of cocaine valued at an estimated $5.8 million from a shipping container in southeast Vancouver the largest such seizure in the city. Police were called to a Vancouver-based company on July 21 after staff located 14 duffle bags of drugs hidden amongst boxes of t-shirts that formed a legitimate order. Sergeant Travis Fraser of the VPD Drug Unit said the business was shocked and called police right away and is in no way associated with the seized cocaine. The amount of drugs as well as the stamps and packaging clearly indicates organized crime is behind the shipment he said. The investigation showed the shipping container originated in Honduras on May 18 2026 was loaded onto a vessel stopped in Jamaica on June 6 2026 and arrived in Montreal on July 5 2026. Fraser said police believe the cocaine was supposed to be removed prior to its arrival at the company. VPD continues to liaise with law enforcement and port authority counterparts in Canada Honduras Jamaica the United States Drug Enforcement Agency and the RCMP. ### Both Sides: Woodfibre LNG tax settlement
Supporters of the deal argued it would provide stable long-term revenue for local services and infrastructure without raising resident taxes allowing the district to plan capital projects with certainty. They noted the funds would arrive over a decade giving the municipality predictable income that could support roads parks and emergency services in the Sea-to-Sky region. Opponents maintained that the project carries unacceptable environmental and safety risks to the Sea-to-Sky corridor and that accepting the funds would lock the community into supporting expanded LNG operations for a decade. They pointed to potential impacts on air quality marine traffic and emergency response capacity along the narrow corridor between Squamish and Whistler. Both sides accept that the project would generate substantial tax revenue if approved. The district will now seek other revenue options or revised negotiations; no further steps or timelines were stated in the coverage. Council members who voted against the package emphasized that the community retains the ability to pursue different fiscal arrangements that do not tie local finances to a single industrial project for ten years. Those who favored the settlement highlighted that rejecting it removes a concrete revenue stream that had already been negotiated between the district and the company.
